findings.reason: `_read_run_rows` keys its cache by blob sha and skips the fetch for an already-cached sha, so routing it through a batch reader that fetches every blob unconditionally would defeat that cache; it is a deliberately different mechanism, not a copy of the batch loop, and §10's 0.5h node need not absorb it — the plan is only missing a one-line note that the sibling exists and is out of scope.
findings.text: §10 states that "what is duplicated is the batched `git cat-file` blob reader" and confines the duplication to the two batch loops, but `reckon/velocity.py` itself carries a third committed-blob reader, `_read_run_rows`, which fetches run records one `git show` at a time (line 695) on top of `_run_blobs`/`_blob_sha` (lines 652, 642); the reuse map does not name it, so a reader cannot tell whether the new public reader is meant to subsume it

reuse_search-1.reason: the run-row reader keys its cache by blob sha and skips fetches for cached shas, so routing it through an unconditional batch reader would defeat that cache; it is a different mechanism and stays, as the reviewer's own reason states

rubric_items.deep_module: pass and the direction is net-positive — §10 removes two wrappers (`_read_blobs`, the counter's `git`) and promotes one shared reader that hides subprocess spawning, `cat-file --batch` payload construction and header/position parsing behind a single entry point taking an ordered `(revision, path)` spec list. That is the shape the rubric asks for; nothing is spread thinner.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the section moves the duplication onto its owner rather than forking it: `reckon/velocity.py` already owns `git()` and the batch loop, so promoting the reader and the cache root there extends the owner. No second placement path, state reader or scheduler query is introduced.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23. §10 is the only section adding surface and it names the accounting in its own text: `public_definitions` +2 (the promoted reader and the promoted cache root on `reckon/velocity.py`), −1 (the counter's public `git` wrapper), net +1, with a stated reason ("the price of a shared mechanism having a public home"). No cli_options, mcp_views or refusal_families are added.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §10 names the mechanisms it would extend and the duplication it measured, and the code confirms them: the batch loop in `interface_counts._read_blobs` (reckon/interface_counts.py:443) is byte-for-byte the loop in `velocity._plan_metas` (reckon/velocity.py:358), `interface_counts._cache_root` reaches into the underscore-private `velocity._velocity_cache_root` (reckon/interface_counts.py:498), and the counter's `git()` (line 54) is identical to velocity's (line 145). The plan also states why the one other copy — the frozen census under docs/research — keeps its own.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §10 does not add a thin layer over the existing loop; it makes the existing loop the owner and deletes the parallel one. It states why `_plan_metas` cannot simply be extended for the counter (it parses `plan-status`/`plan-archived` and returns metas, not bytes), which is exactly the "why not extend it" justification the item requires.
